Haggis with Neeps and Tatties

Served at: Burns Night Supper

Serves 4-6Prep 25 minCook 1 hour 30 min

Haggis with Neeps and Tatties is the iconic centerpiece of a Burns Night Supper, a celebration of Scotland's national poet, Robert Burns, held annually on January 25th. This hearty, traditional dish, consisting of savory haggis served alongside mashed rutabaga (neeps) and mashed potatoes (tatties), is often ceremoniously presented and addressed with Burns' famous poem, "Address to a Haggis," before being enjoyed.

Ingredients

  • 1 (1.5-2 pound / 680-900g) cooked haggis, typically sold in a synthetic casing
  • 2 pounds (900g) rutabaga (swede), peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
  • 2 pounds (900g) starchy potatoes (e.g., Russet or Maris Piper), peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
  • 4 tablespoons (56g) unsalted butter, divided
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) whole milk or heavy cream, plus more as needed, divided
  • Salt, to taste
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

Method

  1. Prepare the Haggis (Oven Method): Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Remove the haggis from its outer packaging but do not remove the casing. Wrap the haggis tightly in aluminum foil. Place the foil-wrapped haggis in a baking dish with about 1 inch (2.5 cm) of hot water. Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or according to package instructions, until piping hot throughout.
  2. Prepare the Neeps: While the haggis bakes, place the cubed rutabaga in a large pot and cover with cold, salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
  3. Mash the Neeps: Return the drained rutabaga to the hot pot. Add 2 tablespoons (28g) of butter and 2 tablespoons (30ml) of milk or cream. Mash until smooth, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
  4. Prepare the Tatties: In a separate large pot, place the cubed potatoes and cover with cold, salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
  5. Mash the Tatties: Return the drained potatoes to the hot pot. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons (28g) of butter and 2 tablespoons (30ml) of milk or cream. Mash until smooth and creamy, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
  6. Serve: Once the haggis is thoroughly heated, carefully remove it from the foil. Cut open the casing down the middle and spoon out the haggis. Serve immediately alongside generous portions of the mashed neeps and tatties.

Tips

  • For a truly authentic experience, serve with a dram of Scotch whisky. A whisky cream sauce can also be drizzled over the haggis.
  • Ensure the neeps and tatties are well-drained before mashing to prevent a watery consistency.
  • Season generously; the earthy flavors of the rutabaga and potato benefit from good seasoning.
